conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during your stay. I know you’re feeling unwell. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Abdomen… big… hurts… no pain now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your belly is very swollen. We saw that in the ER. Your blood pressure was low too, but it improved after we put in a tube to help empty your stomach.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. We’ll manage your foot pain. You’re on your usual pain meds. We’ll add a patch later if needed. Right now, we’re focused on your belly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did a CT scan. It shows your colon is very dilated—like a balloon—especially in the lower part. But no blockage. We think it’s due to your chronic constipation or a sluggish bowel.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No blockage seen. But we can’t rule out a mass yet. We’ll keep watching. We started antibiotics just in case there’s an infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your white blood cell count was high and you had a fever. Also, your lungs showed some changes on the scan—could be from aspiration. So we’re treating both gut and lungs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Oxygen levels are good. No cough. But we’re being cautious. You’re on IV antibiotics for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. We did an ultrasound on your legs because one looked swollen. No blood clot—good news. But we’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Slight swelling remains, but no clot. You’re still on your blood thinner, so that helps prevent clots.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your belly got more distended yesterday and you spiked a fever. The CT showed worse dilation. We started stronger antibiotics for a possible bowel infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, fever is gone. Your white count is coming down. That’s a good sign the antibiotics are working.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll switch to oral vancomycin for 14 days. Even though your stool test was negative, we think you might have had a gut infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also checked your lungs again. The consolidation is still there, but you’re not coughing. We’ll finish a 7-day course with ciprofloxacin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. But you’re at risk for aspiration due to your swallowing issues. We’re treating it just in case.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, speech therapy confirmed you need thickened liquids and pureed food. And someone must supervise every meal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—your latest CT shows the colon is less dilated. The contrast is moving through. No perforation. This is a big improvement.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Your abdomen is softening. We’ll restart your bowel regimen slowly. Gastroenterology recommends adding Miralax daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it helps draw water into the bowel. We’ll also keep enemas and stool softeners as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your X-ray today shows continued improvement. The bowel is less distended. You passed gas and had a small bowel movement—great signs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Very good. We’re also adding a lidocaine patch to your right foot. You said it helps the pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep it on daily. Apply for up to 12 hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All your labs are improving. White count is normal. No signs of infection. We’re almost done with the pneumonia antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Two more days of cipro. But you’ll continue vancomycin by mouth for two weeks to be safe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re holding your iron pills for now. Infection can interfere with absorption. Restart in two weeks with your doctor’s okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Your hemoglobin is stable. No need to rush.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Another X-ray shows continued improvement. Your bowel is almost back to normal size. You had another bowel movement yesterday—excellent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll plan for discharge tomorrow. You’ll go back to your care facility.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Back to your extended care facility. They’ll continue your care with the new meds and diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Today’s the day. Your abdomen is soft, you’re passing stool, and labs are normal. We’re discharging you with instructions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Continue vancomycin for 14 days, cipro for two more doses, Miralax daily, and the lidocaine patch. Keep thickened liquids and pureed food.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And follow up with your doctor. They’ll check on the pending stool test and schedule a colonoscopy in six weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, to make sure there’s no mass causing the dilation. But for now, you’re doing great.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and keep up the good work.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One more thing—your back ulcers. Keep using the special mattress, turn every few hours, and moisturize your skin twice a day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And when you sit up, use the cushion and don’t stay seated more than an hour at a time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set. The nurse will go over your meds and discharge papers now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Get some rest and keep following the plan.
